quote_A.text: Catalan's constant is irrational.

quote_B.text: Such family results guarantee irrational members without identifying the particular value $\beta(2)$.

notes: Long-standing open question rather than a formally named conjecture; P2 chosen (P1 defensible).

claim_formal: ∀ ν>2 ∃ Q ∀ p,q∈ℤ, q≥Q: |π − p/q| ≥ q^{−ν}; equivalently μ(π) = 2

quote_A.text: The irrationality exponent of \(\pi\) is \(2\).

quote_B.text: We prove the conjecture that the irrationality exponent of π is 2.

notes: Closed statement about π (μ(π)=2), so prefix none; the unpacked form is ∀ν ∃Q ∀p,q. Threshold Q(ν) is explicitly ineffective. Corollary: the Flint–Hills series converges. Rule 7 also fits (record number determined exactly → O1, M9).

claim_formal: ∀ admissible a∈ℤ (a≠−1, a not a square) ∃ c_a>0, x_a ∀ x≥x_a: #{p∈(x,2x): ord_p(a)=p−1} ≥ c_a x/(log x)^2

quote_A.text: there are constants $c_a>0$ and $x_a\ge2$ such that, for every real $x\ge x_a$, \[ \#\{p\text{ prime}:x<p<2x,\ p\nmid a,\ \ord_p(a)=p-1\} \ge c_a\frac{x}{(\log x)^2}

quote_B.text: We prove the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture

notes: Proves the infinitude half of Artin's conjecture, not the predicted density asymptotic. That is a partial settlement, coded O5 (O1 if the infinitude assertion is read as the posed problem). The qualitative reading would be prefix ∀∃^∞ with M1. Secondary: a uniform Hecke zero-free region; a companion gives a simultaneous-primitive-root result conditional on four inputs from the main paper.

claim_formal: ∀ compact IHS Kähler X^{2n}, ∀ line bundle L with c_1(L)≠0 nef and q_X(c_1(L))=0: L is semiample (∃ m, f:X→B with L^m ≅ f^*A, dim B = n)

quote_A.text: every holomorphic line bundle with nonzero nef isotropic first Chern class on a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kähler manifold is semiample

quote_B.text: We prove the strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture

notes: Second headline result: for a projective Lagrangian fibration with normal projective base, the base is ℙ^n (the projective-space base conjecture). Corollary: finitely many deformation types when b_2≥5 (uses EFGMS boundedness). Semiampleness also packages a fibration, so M2 is possible.

claim_formal: ∀^∞ admissible d, ∀ᵍ cubic fourfold X ∈ C_d: X irrational ∧ ∃ K3 surface S with Ku(X) ≃ D^b(S)

quote_A.text: There is an integer \(d_0\) such that, for every admissible \(d>d_0\), a very general cubic fourfold \(X\) in \(\mathcal C_d\) is irrational

quote_B.text: This disproves Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture.

notes: Prefix follows rule 2 (no explicit threshold, so ∀^∞) and rule 3. BUCKETS_PLAN lists 054 as plain ∀ᵍ, dropping the d quantifier. Matrix: a family of counterexamples to Kuznetsov's conjecture (M3); the core assertion is irrationality (M4). The categorical half comes from BLMNPS. Corollaries refute associated-K3 sufficiency and Hilbert-square sufficiency, and show universally trivial CH_0.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth connected complex projective Fano 6-fold X with T_X nef: X ≅ G/P rational homogeneous

quote_A.text: Every smooth connected complex projective Fano variety of dimension six with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.

quote_B.text: resolving the Campana–Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six

notes: Rule 6: one dimension of a general conjecture, so O5. Kanemitsu's ρ>n−5 theorem handles ρ≥2, so the paper does Picard number one: pseudoindex 5 is new, pseudoindex 4 is an independent reproof of Watanabe. Corollary: uniformization of compact Kähler manifolds with nef T_X when dim − q̃ ≤ 6.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2, ∀ f ∈ H^{n/(2(n+1))}(ℝ^n), for a.e. x: lim_{t↓0} e^{itΔ}f(x) = f(x)

quote_A.text: For every $f\in H^{1/3}(\R^2)$ there is a set $E_f\subset\R^2$ of full Lebesgue measure such that

quote_B.text: We resolve the planar Sobolev endpoint of Carleson's convergence problem

notes: Two manuscripts: n=2 and n≥3. With Bourgain's necessity s ≥ n/(2(n+1)), this pins the sharp regularity including the endpoint, so M9 is arguable. The headline assertion itself is endpoint convergence (M1). It settles the remaining equality case of the regularity question, so O1.

claim_formal: ∃ c,C>0 ∃ n_0 ∀ n≥n_0: c·n log n ≤ sup_K θ(K) ≤ C·n log n, for lattice and translative covering density, all and centrally symmetric bodies

quote_A.text: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as $`\Theta(n\log n)`$, for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings.

quote_B.text: Theorem~\ref{thm:main} removes this remaining iterated-logarithmic loss and gives the constant-factor $n\log n$ bound.

notes: Lean CoveringOrder.optimal_order matches the headline; SingleLatticeCovering is the upper half. The upper lattice bound Cn log n is new (record: Li–Liu's loglog loss). The lower translative bound is new and answers Naszódi's universal-linear-bound question negatively (P2/O2 for that manuscript). The full Θ needs Rogers' upper bound and Li–Liu's lattice lower bound, hence full_only_with_prior_results.

claim_formal: ∃ deterministic algorithm ∃ C ∀ mean-payoff game (binary weights, input length L): computes the winning set (and values, optimal positional strategies) in ≤ 2^{C(log(L+2))^2} bit operations

quote_A.text: We give a deterministic algorithm that computes the complete zero-threshold winning set of a finite mean-payoff game with arbitrary signed integer edge weights encoded in binary.

quote_B.text: A polynomial bound for the complete binary input would be a further improvement.

notes: Four manuscripts: deterministic MPG, randomized MPG, stochastic MPG, MPG-parity. The extensions call the deterministic MPG paper through its interface (internal builds_on). The outcome is quasipolynomial progress on a long-open complexity question (polynomial time is still open), so P4/O7. P2/O1 is possible if 'quasipolynomial' is taken as the posed question. Lean: RandomizedMeanPayoff (randomized version, weaker than the deterministic headline) and TruffetCounterexample (a different, secondary result).

claim_formal: ∃ deterministic TM ∃ C,k ∀ prime p, n, s: outputs (T_1..T_n) ∈ Mat_d(F_p)^n, d=O(n^3 s^6), in ≤ C(n+s+log p)^k time, with ∀ field F of char p ∀ nonzero NC formula f of size ≤ s: f(T) ≠ 0 (likewise a rational tuple for char 0)

quote_A.text: For every field $F$ of characteristic $p$ and every nonzero $f\in F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\rangle$ computed by a formula of size at most $s$, the same tuple, viewed over $F$, satisfies \[ f(T_1,\ldots,T_n)\ne0. \]

quote_B.text: In particular, the singleton set $\{\mathbf T_{n,s}\}$ gives a positive solution to the polynomial-size rational-matrix hitting-set problem for characteristic-zero formulas.

notes: Deterministic polynomial-time black-box PIT (hitting point) for noncommutative formulas; Forbes–Shpilka had quasipolynomial size. Reading it as existence of a hitting point gives M2. Lean FormulaHitting covers only the char-0 hitting property of an explicit tuple, without running time or char p (weaker). RationalHitting is the rational-formula hitting list, a different secondary result.

claim_formal: ∀ h≥2: OWL_h has an (h+3)-state one-way NFA, and ∀ 2DFA D with s states recognizing OWL_h: 4(s+2)^2 ≥ 2^{⌊(h−2)/31⌋}

quote_A.text: Every equivalent deterministic two-way automaton with $s$ states satisfies \begin{equation} \label{eq:main-bound} 4(s+2)^2\ge 2^{\lfloor(h-2)/31\rfloor}.

quote_B.text: The latter resolves the Sakoda–Sipser state-succinctness conjecture over growing finite alphabets

notes: Principal result: 1NFA→2DFA exponential lower bound (Sakoda–Sipser). The second result, 2NFA complementation needing exponentially many states, answers an open question (P2/O2), and has its own Lean. The fixed-alphabet version is not addressed, so O5 is possible. The ∃N witness half is suppressed in the prefix. The no-polynomial-bound corollary reads as M4.

claim_formal: ∃R ⊆ CH; more precisely ∃ absolute j: EATR (true ∃x∀y real sentences with circuit-encoded polynomials) ∈ C_jP

quote_A.text: We prove that the existential theory of the reals lies in the counting hierarchy.

quote_B.text: Our theorem places this two-block language in a fixed level of the counting hierarchy.

notes: Prefix: the headline is a closed statement about named classes (ETR ∈ CH); the main theorem reads ∃j EATR ∈ C_jP. The explicit bound ETR ∈ C_26 P is secondary. The input lacks an explicit statement that ETR ⊆ CH was a posed question. P2 is assumed (classical gap PSPACE vs CH); P5 is possible.

claim_formal: ∀ λ∈(0,1): ν_λ singular ⇔ λ ∈ 𝒞 (an explicit limsup-of-algebraic-unit-approximation set)

quote_A.text: For every $\lambda\in(0,1)$, the measure $\nu_\lambda$ is singular if and only if $\lambda\in\mathcal C$

quote_B.text: The classification problem asks which of these alternatives holds for each parameter, including exceptional parameters.

notes: The criterion is an infinite approximation condition, not an algorithm, so whether it 'settles' the classification problem is debatable (O1 at low confidence; P5/new result is an alternative). Second headline: singularity at reciprocals of every quartic Salem number and at one degree-31 non-Pisot root. This answers the recorded open question on non-Pisot singular examples (P2/O2-type, via existence, M2/M3).

claim_formal: ∀ d≥3 ∃ c_d>0 ∀ finite P⊂ℝ^d, |P|=n≥2: |Δ(P)| ≥ c_d n^{2/d}

quote_A.text: every finite set \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) of \(n\ge2\) distinct points satisfies \[ |\Delta(P)|\ge c_d n^{2/d}. \]

quote_B.text: This resolves the higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture positively.

notes: The integer grid makes the order n^{2/d} sharp (classical), so M9 is arguable under the attainment precedence. The headline is a one-sided lower bound, so M8. Uses the Guth–Katz planar bound as the base of the induction.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥3 ∃ deterministic algorithm, k_d, n_0(d) ∀ even n≥n_0: outputs in O_d(n^{k_d}) time a simple d-regular graph on n vertices with all nontrivial eigenvalues in (−2√(d−1), 2√(d−1))

quote_A.text: the algorithm outputs the adjacency list of a simple $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in $O_d(n^{k_d})$ bit operations

quote_B.text: These exact constructions do not cover every fixed degree and every prescribed large order simultaneously.

notes: An explicit construction is algorithm existence (M10); M2 is the alternative, since the existence of such graphs at the specified sizes is itself new for nonbipartite graphs. restricted_range reflects even n only. The problem posed in the input is implicit (deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every degree), so P2.

claim_formal: ∃ binary 66×66 matrix H ∀ c,C>0 ∃ n, ε, A ∈ {0,1}^{n×n}: dist_H(A) ≥ ε ∧ N_H(A) < c ε^C n^{132}

quote_A.text: There is a fixed binary $66\times66$ matrix $H$ with the following property.

quote_B.text: This disproves the polynomial ordered binary matrix-removal conjecture.

notes: Conjecture 4.5 of Gishboliner–Shapira (arXiv v1); also Alon–Ben-Eliezer Problem 1.4. H is explicit in Lean (fixedH), but rule 1 keeps ∃. Corollary: canonical testers need exp(Ω(ε^{−1/2})) queries.

claim_formal: ∀ prime p ∀ finite group G ∀ p-block B of G: l(B) = |W_p(B)|

quote_A.text: For every prime $p$, every finite group $G$, and every $p$-block $B$ of $G$, \[ l(B)=|W_p(B)|. \]

quote_B.text: We prove the numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for every finite group and every prime p.

notes: Matrix: an equality of two invariants. It is coded M7 (identity of named quantities); M1 (property holds) is equally plausible. Corollaries: Alperin's local–global bounds, and principal-block bounds of Hung–Sambale–Tiep.

claim_formal: ∀ infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive G with h_V(G)>0: p_c(G) < p_{2→2}(G) ≤ p_u(G)

quote_A.text: \pc(G)<\ptwo(G)\le\pu(G)

quote_B.text: We prove the bond-percolation nonuniqueness conjecture of Benjamini and Schramm

notes: Also proves Hutchcroft's operator-threshold conjecture (p_c < p_{2→2}). Corollaries: the critical triangle condition, mean-field exponents, and the Cayley graph case. The Lean full_main contains the headline plus the operator statement.

claim_formal: ℙ: for the half-plane Temperleyan double-dimer law, F(𝓛_δ) ⇒ nested CLE_4 as δ↓0, in the loop-collection (curve) topology

quote_A.text: \[ F(\mathcal L_\delta)\ \Longrightarrow\ F(\mathcal L), \qquad \delta\downarrow0, \] where \(\mathcal L\) is standard nested \(\CLE_4\) in \(\HH\).

quote_B.text: This resolves the half-plane Temperleyan form of the double-dimer CLE4 scaling-limit conjecture.

notes: Matrix: a scaling-limit identification. Coded M7 (limit equals a named object); no code fits cleanly, and M1 is possible. Rule 4 gives ℙ. One domain and boundary form of a general conjecture, so O5 by rule 6. It upgrades Basok–Chelkak's cylindrical (topological) convergence to curve convergence, hence full_only_with_prior_results.

claim_formal: Thorp shuffle on n=2^d cards: ‖q_d^{*(1600d)} − U_n‖_TV → 0 as d→∞ (worst start), and t_mix(d) ≥ 2d − O(1); hence t_mix(d) = Θ(d) = Θ(log N)

quote_A.text: Consequently the mixing time at distance $1/4$ satisfies

quote_B.text: The corresponding optimal-order question for arbitrary even deck sizes is not addressed by the cube argument here.

notes: Prefix: rule 4 (limit statement about a random process) gives ℙ; ∀^∞ is the alternative. M9: order determined (Θ). Problem: the optimal (logarithmic) mixing order, previously O(d^3) (Morris). This could be P4/O1 (record determined). Coded O5 because only dyadic decks are covered. Thirteen manuscripts give alternative proofs and intermediate estimates. Lean BinarySweep proves only the O(d) upper bound (a fixed number of sweeps mixes), so weaker. The other Lean comparators are intermediate results. full_only_with_prior_results is weak: the lower bound is a support count.

claim_formal: ∀ finitely generated group G: (G has decidable word problem) ⇔ (∃ finitely presented simple H, G ↪ H)

quote_A.text: For every finitely generated group \(G\), the following are equivalent

quote_B.text: We prove the Boone–Higman conjecture.

notes: Companion results: the simple overgroup can be of type F∞ (higher-finiteness strengthening, with its own Lean, SimpleOvergroups), and a universal F∞ group contains all finitely presented groups (answers FFZ Question 1.3; Lean UniversalFInfinity). The Lean BooneHigman.main is the headline equivalence.

claim_formal: ∀ γ∈(1/2,3/2) ∀ m≥1 ∀ W:ℝ→H_m^+ with ∫tr W^{γ+1/2}<∞: Tr(H_W)_-^γ ≤ C_γ ∫ tr W^{γ+1/2}, C_γ = the scalar one-bound-state constant, attained; equality iff W is a constant-unitary direct sum of sech² solitons and zero channels

quote_A.text: The constant is optimal in every matrix dimension.

quote_B.text: We resolve affirmatively the remaining cases of the scalar one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring conjecture

notes: Three manuscripts: scalar 1D LT conjecture for 1/2<γ<3/2 (the classical P1 target), its matrix-valued extension (headline), and the classification of all equality cases (M6-type secondary). Settling the scalar conjecture gives O1; seen from the matrix headline it extends a theorem (O8). Lean covers only the scalar case (m=1), so weaker.

claim_formal: PARITY ∉ QAC^0: ∀ d, c≥1, ε>0 ∃ n_0 ∀ n≥n_0 ∀ depth-≤d circuits on ≤ n^c qubits (1-qubit gates + unbounded Toffoli) ∀ output qubit ∃ x: Pr[out = ⊕x] < 1/2+ε

quote_A.text: For all sufficiently large \(n\), no circuit of depth at most \(d\) on \(n\) input qubits and at most \(n^c\) total qubits

quote_B.text: This resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model.

notes: Prefix: the headline is a closed separation about named objects (parity, QAC0), so none. The unpacked Lean prefix is ∀∀^∞∀∃. The measured-output model is more permissive than Moore's clean-ancilla model, so the result covers the original; O1. Corollary via Xu–Li: strict majority is also not in QAC0. Two independent proofs (two manuscripts); both Lean comparators match.

claim_formal: ∀ Γ∈𝒦 (ICC, commensurable with a property-(T) lattice over char-0 local fields) ∀ ICC Λ ∀ cocycles μ,ω ∀ bifinite L_μ(Γ)–L_ω(Λ) correspondence H: H is a summand of a finite sum of models E(A,B,δ,σ) from finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and projective representations

quote_A.text: Every such correspondence is a closed summand of a finite direct sum of models obtained from actual finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and finite-dimensional projective representations of the matched cocycle ratio.

quote_B.text: his later problems ask whether nonisomorphic ICC property-$(T)$ groups have nonisomorphic factors

notes: The summary poses no problem. The companion recovers stable isomorphisms (group, cocycle, amplification), which addresses Connes' rigidity problems and Popa's stable form for this lattice class only. Hence P1/O5 at low confidence; P5 (new result) is an alternative reading.

claim_formal: ∃ n≥2 ∃ bounded self-adjoint n-tuple X in a tracial vN algebra: −∞ < χ(X) ≤ χ*(X) − 1/2 < ∞

quote_A.text: There exist an integer $n\geq2$ and a bounded self-adjoint tuple $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$

quote_B.text: We answer the finite-entropy equality question for microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy negatively.

notes: Guionnet states it as Conjecture 7.1; the summary calls it Voiculescu's question, so P1 vs P2 is ambiguous. The number n of variables is large but fixed; smaller n is not addressed.

claim_formal: ∀ finite group G ∀ prime p: O_p(G)=1 → H̃_*(A_p(G);ℚ) ≠ 0

quote_A.text: For every finite group $G$ and every prime $p$, if $\Op(G)=1$, then \[ \widetilde H_*(\Ap(G);\Q)\ne0. \]

quote_B.text: We prove Quillen's conjecture for all finite groups and all primes.

notes: This proves the stronger rational-homology form, which implies Quillen's contractibility conjecture. It relies heavily on prior reductions (Aschbacher–Kleidman, Aschbacher–Smith, Piterman–Smith, Díaz Ramos for odd p, Piterman for p=2). The paper supplies the remaining unitary and p=2 steps.

claim_formal: ∀ nonzero real Banach X,Y ∀ surjective isometry f:S_X→S_Y: T(x)=‖x‖f(x/‖x‖) is a surjective real-linear isometry, and the unique linear extension of f

quote_A.text: is a surjective real-linear isometry. It is the unique linear extension of $f$.

quote_B.text: giving an affirmative solution to Tingley's problem

notes: The extension is explicit (the radial map); rule 1 keeps ∃!. M1 (the radial map has a property) is the alternative. Tingley's problem is the plan's example of P2.

claim_formal: ∃ C^∞ positive-definite metric g on (−1,1)^2 ∀ open U∋0 ∀ C^∞ F:U→ℝ^3: F is not an isometric immersion of (U,g)

quote_A.text: There is a \(C^\infty\) positive definite Riemannian metric \(g\) on \((-1,1)^2\) such that no open neighborhood \(U\) of the origin admits a \(C^\infty\) isometric immersion

quote_B.text: This gives a negative answer to the unrestricted smooth local isometric realization problem for surfaces.

notes: Rule 5: a counterexample to a universal question, so M3. The question appears as Problem 1.9 in Ghomi's survey and in Yau's discussion. Ghomi's survey is a problem collection, so P3 is arguable; rule 8 gives P2. Corollary: the metric can be flat to infinite order at 0. Sign-restricted cases (K≥0 or K≤0) remain open.

claim_formal: ∀ m,n≥1 ∀ open U⊂ℝ^{m+n} ∀ stationary integral m-varifold V in U: dim_H Sing V ≤ m−1

quote_A.text: \[ \dim_{\Hh}\Sing V\le m-1. \]

quote_B.text: This sharp bound proves the Euclidean singular-set conjecture recorded by Brena, Decio, and De Lellis.

notes: The bound is attained by two m-planes crossing along an (m−1)-plane, so M9 under the precedence rule; M8 if the attainment is read as classical. Companion: H^m(Sing V)=0 (BDD Conjecture 1.2), implied by the dimension bound, with a round-sphere corollary.

claim_formal: ∃ closed connected orientable smooth 3-manifold M: (∃ metric without conjugate points on M) ∧ ¬(∃ metric of sectional curvature ≤ 0 on M)

quote_A.text: There exists a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold $M$ with a $C^\infty$ Riemannian metric without conjugate points

quote_B.text: We give a negative answer in dimension three

notes: Question of Ivanov–Kapovitch (Questions 1.1 and 8.1) and Burns–Matveev (Question 4.1.2). A counterexample in dimension 3 answers the general question negatively, and the survey poses the 3-dimensional case explicitly; hence O2, not O5. Extra: π_1(M) has no proper cocompact CAT(0) action, and M has no metric without focal points.

claim_formal: ∀ n≥2 ∀ p,q>0 ∀ A,B∈ℝ with (n+A)/(p+1)+(n+B)/(q+1) > n−2: ¬∃ u,v ∈ C^2(ℝ^n∖0)∩C(ℝ^n), u,v>0, with −Δu=|x|^A v^p, −Δv=|x|^B u^q

quote_A.text: There are no functions \[ u,v\in C^2(\R^n\setminus\{0\})\cap C(\R^n), \qquad u(x)>0,\quad v(x)>0\quad(x\in\R^n), \]

quote_B.text: We prove the subcritical Hénon–Lane–Emden conjecture

notes: Resolves Huang–Zou's Conjecture B. Corollary: the unweighted Lane–Emden conjecture (A=B=0). Combined with Bidaut-Véron–Giacomini radial existence, it gives Phan's Conjecture C in full (an existence classification).
